passage:
You ask if you're foolish to keep calling someone who hardly ever calls you back. I'm Jahnavi, so let me tell you about Rafiq. We were close at college. For six years I rang him every month; he rang me twice. I told myself loyalty means never counting.

Then, on my birthday, I noticed I was tired and bitter. So I did what I should have done sooner and asked him plainly, "Do you want this friendship to be closer? I'd love that, and it's fine if not."

He said his life was full but he cared about me; he simply wasn't a caller. We settled on two visits a year. I stopped waiting for the phone. Some friendships live at a lower flame, and without resentment they last.

qa.q: How many times did Rafiq ring Jahnavi in six years?
qa.a: Rafiq rang twice, while Jahnavi rang every month.

qa.q: What was Jahnavi feeling on the birthday?
qa.a: Tired and bitter after years of believing loyalty means never counting.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi do to check whether the effort was mutual?
qa.a: Jahnavi asked Rafiq plainly whether he wanted a closer friendship, then accepted his answer of two visits a year.

qa.q: How did Rafiq see the friendship?
qa.a: Rafiq said his life was full but he cared about Jahnavi, and that he simply wasn't a caller.

grounding: Loyal calling to a friend who rarely calls back leads Jahnavi to check whether effort is mutual and let the friendship find its natural level.
